component.name: Weir
component.summary: Mix and route microphones and applications

description.p: Weir puts the sound on your computer on a mixing desk, in the style of Voicemeeter. Your microphone, your music, your browser and your game each get a strip with a fader. Your headphones, your speakers and a virtual microphone for Discord or OBS each get a bus. A row of buttons beside every fader decides who hears what.

ul.li: As many strips and buses as you need, each a device other programs can choose
A separate mix for every output, so a strip can be louder in your headphones than on your stream
Noise suppression, a noise gate, a compressor and a 16-band equalizer for voices
Ducking, which turns the music down while you talk, and a safety limiter on every output
Surround sound up to 7.1
External effects: send a strip or bus through another program, such as Carla, and back
Hotkeys for anything the mixer does, such as push to talk
Scenes, setups, rules for where applications go, and undo
Export your settings to a file, to keep or to move to another computer
A command line and a documented protocol, for scripts and stream decks

screenshot.caption: The mixer: strips on the left, buses on the right
A strip's noise gate, compressor and equalizer

description.p: Hotkeys, settings you can take to another computer, and setups and scenes that each do one thing.

ul.li: Hotkeys: keyboard shortcuts for anything the mixer does, such as push to talk, muting a strip or loading a scene. They work with the window closed and in full-screen games, can be put in order and in groups, and show in Plasma's System Settings.
Export your scenes, setups, hotkeys, equalizer presets, app rules and preferences to a file, and import all of them or just a few, on this computer or another.
A setup is now which strips and buses there are, and a scene how they sound. Load a setup alone, or with any scene from the Setups menu. Each old setup's mix becomes a scene of the same name.
Each bus can be delayed by up to half a second, to line up outputs that lag, such as a Bluetooth speaker. Contributed by SemmyEM.
The fields in the strip and bus menus can be clicked and typed into.
App rules keep their strip by name, so a rule waits for a setup that has its strip.

description.p: External effects: a strip or bus can send its sound to another program, such as Carla or EasyEffects, for effects Weir does not have, and take it back to carry on through the mix.

ul.li: Switch them on in a strip's or bus's settings, and drag them to any point of its signal chain.
A badge beside the name shows at a glance whether the effects program is connected.
Choose whether the sound passes through unchanged or stays silent while nothing is connected.
Links of Weir's own that are removed in a patchbay are made again.

description.p: Fixes for starting Weir when you log in:

ul.li: The tray icon appears even when Weir starts before the desktop's panel.
The mixer window opens at login.
Only one mixer window opens. Starting Weir again brings the open one to the front.
The window no longer freezes while it is minimized, which kept it from closing at shutdown.

description.p: Weir is now also packaged for Arch Linux and the systems built on it, and for Fedora and Nobara on COPR. Weir itself is unchanged.
